hypotheses_validated.claim: hx_f32_to_f16 / hx_f32_to_bf16 are exact round-to-nearest-even for every f32 input (subnormals, overflow to inf, NaN stays NaN with F16C / AVX512-BF16 quieting), and f16/bf16 -> f32 is exact for all 65536 patterns.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_platform --exhaustive: all 2^32 inputs vs an independent nearest-neighbour reference (ldexp value tables + binary search, ties to even pattern): 0 mismatches for both formats (11.3 s, 32 threads). The default run checks all 65536 decode/round-trip patterns, every rounding boundary (each representable value, each midpoint, midpoint +-1 ulp, both signs) and 4M random inputs per format.

hypotheses_validated.claim: On Windows a handle opened WITHOUT FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED serialises concurrent positional reads in the I/O manager, so reader threads cannot raise NVMe queue depth.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Scratch benchmark on the Samsung 990 PRO, FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING, random reads over a 4 GiB file: synchronous handle 64 KiB 0.62-0.64 GB/s at 1/4/8/16 threads (flat), 1 MiB ~3.9 GB/s flat; overlapped handle 64 KiB 0.65/2.46/4.19/5.73 GB/s, 1 MiB 4.0/6.8/5.9/5.9 GB/s at 1/4/8/16 threads. Measured while other engineers were running builds (noisy).

hypotheses_validated.claim: hx_file_pread through the overlapped design scales with reader threads, and single-thread throughput equals raw Win32.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Scratch bench via hx_file API, direct: 64 KiB 0.31/2.01/3.72/4.12 GB/s at 1/4/8/16 threads, 1 MiB 2.2/6.4/5.8/5.9, 4 MiB 4.4/5.8/5.9/6.2. A back-to-back rerun gave single-thread 0.61-0.63 GB/s (64 KiB) and 3.91 GB/s (1 MiB), the same as raw sync/overlapped Win32 in the same session. Noisy machine.

hypotheses_validated.claim: hx_pool_run round trip (empty task) is about 1 us with 16 threads while workers spin, and no wake-up is lost on the sleep path.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_pool (MSVC /O2, Windows 11, 9950X, noisy): 16 threads spin_us=1000 mean 0.78-0.98 us, p50 0.6-0.9 us, p99 1.2-1.5 us; 4 threads mean 0.15-0.46 us; 200k back-to-back dispatches at 4 and 16 threads and 20k at 16 threads with spin_us=0 (pure sleep/wake path) all verified every tid ran exactly once. Linux (WSL2, gcc 13.3): 16 threads p50 0.66-0.78 us.

hypotheses_validated.claim: The POSIX implementation (platform_posix.c) compiles warning-free and passes the same tests on Linux.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04, gcc 13.3: -std=c11 -ffp-contract=off -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-parameter, -O2 and -O1 -fsanitize=address,undefined (LeakSanitizer on): test_platform (with --expect-cpu incl. cores=16,cpus=32) and test_pool --quick pass, no sanitizer reports. macOS/BSD branches are NOT compiled anywhere (read-only review).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Contributor tests detect breakage (mutation testing, governance/tools/mutate.py, 60 sampled mutants each, seed 1).
hypotheses_validated.evidence: pool.c 73.3% (test_pool --quick); platform_common.inc 86.7% (run on a scratch copy renamed to .h because mutate.py rejects .inc); platform_win.c 75.0% (test_platform --expect-cpu ...). Every survivor was reviewed: timing-equivalent spin/caller-wait variants, leaks (MSVC ASan has no leak checker), unreachable fallbacks (thread-creation failure, malloc failure, GetActiveProcessorCount==0), the large-page path (privilege not held), the GCC-only cpuid branch (not compiled by MSVC), and feature-bit '&&'->'||' mutants that are equivalent on a CPU that has every bit.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Periodically yielding (SwitchToThread every 20 us) inside the spin loops improves dispatch latency when the pool has as many threads as logical CPUs.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Scratch A/B, 2 rounds each: 32 threads p50 1.1 us without yield vs 23-42 us with yield; means were noisy either way (23-115 us vs 30-111 us). Kept the plain spin.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: CREATE_WAITABLE_TIMER_HIGH_RESOLUTION gives sub-100 us sleeps on this Windows 11 machine.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Measured: requests of 20-200 us return after ~0.28-0.5 ms (min) / ~0.5 ms (avg); 1 ms -> 1.0-1.5 ms. Still far better than Sleep(1) (~2 ms). hx_sleep_us never returns early, but overshoots by up to ~0.5 ms.

open_questions: Pools with n_threads == logical CPUs (32 here) suffer whenever another process preempts a worker: p50 ~1 us but mean 20-380 us and p99 ~1 ms on this shared machine. Callers should keep the default n_threads = physical cores (hearth.h already does).
MEM_LARGE_PAGES path is untested: SeLockMemoryPrivilege is not held on this machine, so hx_alloc_large(.., 1) silently used normal pages (confirmed with HEARTH_LOG=3).
O_DIRECT fallback on Linux was not exercised: WSL2's 6.6 kernel accepts O_DIRECT even on tmpfs (/dev/shm), so the EINVAL path never triggered.

On Linux, O_DIRECT is accepted at open() time but a filesystem with a logical block size > 4096 would fail reads with EINVAL; Windows checks FileStorageInfo and falls back, POSIX does not (could use statx STATX_DIOALIGN on Linux >= 6.1).
